instructions: For the marinade, mince 3 of the garlic cloves and the shallot. Stir them in a large bowl with the turmeric, 2 tbsp of the oil, 1 1/2 tsp of the fish sauce, the salt and 1/2 tsp of the sugar.
Pat the tilapia dry and cut it into 2-inch pieces. Toss it in the marinade and leave it for 10 minutes while you do the next steps.

For the dipping sauce, mince the remaining 2 garlic cloves. Stir them in a small bowl with 3 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp fish sauce, the vinegar, the juice of the lime and 1/4 cup warm water until the sugar dissolves. Slice the chili into a separate small dish for the table.
Put the vermicelli in a heatproof bowl and cover with just-boiled water. Let it stand for 4 minutes, then drain and divide among four bowls.
Slice the onion. Cut the scallions into 2-inch pieces and the dill into 2-inch pieces, stems and all.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add half the fish in a single layer. Leave it for 2 minutes, until golden underneath, then flip each piece and cook for 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the rest.
Wipe the pan. Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the onion and half the scallions over medium-high heat. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Add half the dill and toss for 30 seconds, until it wilts.
Return the fish to the pan with the rest of the scallions and dill. Fold gently for 1 minute, until it's warmed through and the fish flakes.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more fish sauce.
Serve the fish and pan juices over the noodles, with the dipping sauce and the sliced chili on the side.
method_notes: Posh Journal leads (5 from 15 ratings), with Marion's Kitchen (4.9 from 9) close behind. Both coat white fish in a turmeric, garlic and fish sauce marinade, pan-fry it, and finish with a big handful of dill and scallions over rice noodles with nuoc cham. Posh Journal marinates 30 minutes and adds peanuts; Marion's Kitchen adds curry powder and cooks with no wait. This version marinates only 10 minutes so it fits a 30-minute lunch, leaves out the peanuts to stay nut-free, and takes the dipping sauce from Marion's Kitchen with the chili moved to the table.
